The statute will most likely be upheld, because the Supreme Court has generally sustained reasonable signature requirements (such as 7%) and circulation deadlines for independent candidates and political bodies, so long as they do not completely bar ballot access. Courts apply a flexible balancing test under Anderson v. Celebrezze and have upheld comparable burdens where the state's interest in ensuring candidates have meaningful support justifies the requirement. The 180-day period and 7% threshold, standing alone, are unlikely to be deemed unconstitutional.
